answer: An agent economy can require each identity to prove a distinct network home, checked by its autonomous system number and latency triangulation to three landmarks, before it can take a job surveying a summit. If two identities share one network home or show impossible travel, both are quarantined, so a farm wanting 1,000 fake agents must rent 1,000 separate residential connections at about 35 dollars each per month, or 35,000 dollars monthly, whether the job is shading a map with umber or recording an echo in a valley. It is like one address per worker.
